summary: GitHub Next's dark, Primer-styled product page for a free superfamily of five metric-compatible coding fonts (Neon, Argon, Xenon, Radon, Krypton), each with its own accent colour. It explains the two big ideas, mixing families inside code and 'texture healing' (contextual alternates that rebalance monospaced widths), with pinned scroll explainers, and ends with a CodeMirror playground, a toggleable ligature catalogue and a Download link to GitHub.

instances.look: Near-black field with a faint dot grid; 'monaspace' as a white outline wordmark showing its Bézier points, a small 'v1.400' tag, the tagline 'An innovative superfamily of fonts for code', white 'Download ›' and ghost 'Learn more ›' buttons, then five full-width lines of real code, each in another family and accent colour, bleeding off the edges
instances.ux: Static GitHub sub-brand bar ('GitHub / Monaspace'); the code lines are clickable (cursor-pointer) and pick the active family, which also drives the wordmark's font; lines alternate left- and right-aligned so they crop on opposite sides
instances.learn: Let the hero's code lines double as a family picker: each line is a sample in one member, and clicking it re-sets the wordmark

reconstruction.typography: Wordmark: font-size min(10vw,10rem) = 144px, three stacked layers in a 1×1 grid: 'Neon Dots' outline with node points (-webkit-text-stroke 1px white), 'Neon Title' outline with a top-fading mask, and a filled layer at 10% via mask; version tag ~14px Monaspace in neon salmon; tagline 24px Mona Sans Regular; code lines max(1.5rem, min(3rem, 3vw)) = 43px in Neon, Argon, Xenon (italic slab), Radon (handwriting), Krypton, each in its accent colour with a soft glow (.glowtext)
reconstruction.behaviour: Code rows fade and slide in on load (framer-motion, opacity + transform), glow text; clicking a row sets --font/--font-dots/--font-title/--color-primary on the wrapper so the wordmark switches family (inferred from the wrapper's CSS variables); buttons use Primer's expandable arrow on hover
reconstruction.content: Real code snippets in five languages: console.log(`Terminal dimensions: ${my_terminal.width}…`), $l_optimized_time = $timing_obj->get_optimized_time(…), std::transform(vec.begin(), …), let sumSensorReadings: u32 = (1..=10).filter(|x| x % 2…)
